content:
First, what I suggest you do in the future is run periodic backups. No software, no computer, can be 100% safe, especially since no one can predict the combinations of software and hardware. Second, your problem may simply be that thunderbird reset the profile, which would mean your profile may still be sitting there on your computer. You can check that by these steps:

  1. click help>troubleshootinginformation
  2. scroll to 'profile folder' and click 'open folder'
  3. backup one folder so that you are looking at Profile folder
  4. look in the folder at all stored profiles. The one with your data will have recent dates. If your account is IMAP, look in the imapmail folder, otherwise the Mail folder
  5. once you have located the folder, post back and we will help you set it back up

Then, on your final request, you can install eM Client or Mailbird, both of which can automatically import your accounts.

As a comment, you are responsible for what happened. Yes, you. You have the ability to set Thunderbird and Firefox to NOT AUTOMATICALLY UPDATE, you let both update automatically, and then complain.. And doing backups would prevent the entire scenario. We're glad to help. You can too. Thank you.
creator: davidsk

content:
If addressbook is gone, usually there is more that is gone. But I'll bypass that. What may have happened is that a new profile was created. To check that,

  1. click help>troubleshootinginformation
  2. scroll to 'profile folder' and click 'open folder'
  3. scroll back one folder to the Profiles folder'
  4. look at each profile folder stored in that folder, the files would be abook.sqlite and history.sqlite. Find the ones with most recent dates.
  5. once you locate them, you can either use Windows file manager and copy to your profile folder (with thunderbird not running) or use the import feature you mentioned to recover them.

This approach has been successful:

  4. you are now in the profile folder. copy ALL of it and save to external media **

  6. repeat steps 1 through 3 above
  7. delete the contents of the profile
  8. paste the contents of the profile you copied from other PC
  9. if there is a compatibility.ini file, rename it
  10. restart thunderbird

This completely moves everything. The linux PC should have same or newer release of thunderbird.
